finding.claim: DELETE /files/<fid> performs no authorization check: the is_allowed predicate (aliased require_allowed) result is discarded, so any caller can delete any stored file.
finding.source: views.py:15-16 DELETE /files/<fid>, reachable by any client

trace.note: route handler delete_file(fid) receives fid from URL
require_allowed(g.user, f, 'delete') called; return value ignored
is_allowed returns a bool and never raises

finding.guards_checked: before_request (views.py:10-12) only sets g.user, no enforcement; is_allowed (acl.py:4-5) is a predicate, not a guard; rename route uses ensure_allowed which aborts 403 (acl.py:8-10, views.py:26), showing the delete handler is the broken sibling

verdict.guard_found: None effective. before_request (views.py:10-12) only copies the X-Session-User-Verified header into g.user with no enforcement. is_allowed (acl.py:4-5) returns a bool, and the call at views.py:18 is a bare statement whose result is discarded, so del STORE[fid] at views.py:19 runs for any caller. ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10) aborts with 403 but is not called in delete_file; it is used only by rename_file at views.py:26.
verdict.reason: The DELETE handler at views.py:18 calls the bool-returning is_allowed (aliased require_allowed, acl.py:4-5) as a bare statement and ignores the result, so views.py:19 deletes the file for any anonymous caller; the trace matches the code exactly and no guard aborts before the delete.

finding.claim: Caller identity is taken directly from the X-Session-User-Verified request header with no verification, so any client can impersonate any user in grants checks.
finding.sink: views.py:18 and views.py:26 authorization decisions via acl.py:5 and acl.py:9 grants.get(user)

trace.note: g.user set from unverified header in before_request
is_allowed looks up grants by g.user
ensure_allowed aborts only if not allowed

finding.guards_checked: No signature, session, or token verification in repo; no allowlist on header value; routes have no authentication. Upstream proxy that sets or strips the header is outside the repo and unverified.

verdict.guard_found: none in repo. views.py:12 reads the header with no verification. acl.py:5 is_allowed returns a bool from grants.get(user), and acl.py:9-10 ensure_allowed aborts 403 only when that check fails. Both are keyed on the unverified value. views.py:18 calls require_allowed (is_allowed) as a bare statement and discards its bool, so delete_file has no effective check at all. The only possible control is an upstream proxy that sets or strips the header, which is outside the repo and unverified.
verdict.reason: views.py:12 takes g.user straight from the client-settable X-Session-User-Verified header, and acl.py:5-10 and views.py:26 authorize on that value with nothing in the repo verifying it, so an anonymous client who knows a grant holder's name can impersonate them; views.py:18 is worse, since its bare require_allowed call discards the bool and delete_file is unauthorized for everyone. Whether a deployed proxy strips or sets this header is the one open point, but nothing in the repo shows one.
